gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: ___ money was spent on advertising last year.
Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ in a bad mood.
gaps.explanation: 'Mostly' is an adverb meaning mainly or usually; 'most' as a quantifier needs a noun.

gaps.sentence: She carried a suitcase in ___ hand.
gaps.explanation: 'Each hand' views the two hands individually; 'every hand' is not used for body parts this way.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with rude customers.
___ smells burnt in here — can you check the oven?
gaps.hint: affirmative statement about an unknown thing
gaps.explanation: 'Something' is used in affirmative sentences for an unknown thing; the request to check the oven shows the speaker believes it.

gaps.sentence: We need to find ___ who can fix the boiler.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement: an unknown but existing person
gaps.explanation: 'Someone' is used in affirmative sentences; 'anyone' belongs to questions and negatives.
